meaning: The comment claims the old M4 jugular column was not comparable to the patient columns, because the generic deck ran a 160 s Pext ramp while the patient créneaux run to ~418 s, and asserts the fix is one M4 jugular run per patient schedule while the abdominal ramp and tilt can keep a single shared M4 run.

could_move.what: The numbers 160.0, 418.37 and 418.75 and the ends_early flag are stated in prose; if the patient créneaux schedules change, the comment becomes wrong and the comparability argument silently stales.
The claim that compression window and amplitude are per-patient drives the need for Model_3/run_jc_patients.jl; if that is not actually per-patient, the extra runs are unnecessary.

The claim that abdominal ramp and tilt schedules are identical across models and patients means those columns stay built from one shared M4 run; if Protocol.jl differs per patient anywhere, those columns are not like-for-like.
M5 patients 137 and 150 are said to be fitted but not simulated, which is why they appeared in the payload missing array; that state may already have changed.

expectation: If the claim holds, per-patient M4 jugular runs should end near 418 s instead of 160 s, and the animation should show four patient columns instead of two. The size of the change in the compared curves is unknown from this context.

check.why: Prints the planned runs and their schedules without re-fitting, so a reader can see whether one M4 jugular run per patient is emitted and whether abdominal/tilt still share one run. The reach trace found no references or decks for this script, so I could not confirm a --dry-run flag exists; if it does not, the command fails fast and cheaply.
